raw_response:
I have been farming this land for fifty years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather like I know my own hands. My farm is 5 mu — not big, but it is mine, and it is enough for two of us with some to sell.

I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on 3.5 mu. This is what I have always done. Wheat in winter fills the grain bin and maize in summer brings in money. These two crops I can manage mostly myself. My wife helps during busy seasons. I do not need to take risks — I just need a steady harvest.

For cotton I will plant 1.5 mu on the other piece of land. Cotton earns more per mu than grain, and I have always grown some. But at my age, picking cotton three or four times through the heat of September is very hard. I will not plant more than 1.5 mu. That is the most my body can manage.

For wheat, I will use the improved variety from the county seed station — the same one I used last year, it gave good ears. I apply base fertilizer before planting and top-dress urea at jointing. Three irrigations: winter water before freezing, again at jointing, again at heading. I have seen what happens when farmers skip the jointing water — the stalks fall over. Two spray treatments, one for weeds early, one for aphids near heading.

For maize I always use hybrid seed — even I know hybrid gives a bigger cob. I rotary-till lightly after wheat harvest and sow straight away. Two irrigations if summer rain is short. One herbicide spray early, one for pests later.

For cotton I plough deep in spring to break up the clay layer. Improved seed, not the expensive hybrid — I do not want to spend too much. Cotton needs more potassium so I add extra. Four irrigations spaced through the summer. Five pesticide sprays — bollworm and mites will destroy the bolls if I am not careful.
